nodes.label: Pacman moves one tile per step in the requested direction
A move into a wall tile is refused and pacman stays put
Moving onto a dot or power pellet eats it and adds to the score, a pellet being worth more than a dot; a pellet also frightens every ghost
Touching a ghost costs a life, unless the ghost is frightened, in which case it is eaten for points
The game is won once every dot and pellet is eaten
The game is lost once the last life is spent; otherwise pacman and the ghosts respawn
WASD and the arrow keys both drive the same four directions
The canvas rescales to the viewport, keeping the maze's aspect ratio and pixel-art sharpness
Each tick, every ghost advances one walkable step toward pacman when chasing and away from pacman when frightened
Pressing P or p while the game is being played pauses it, and pressing it again resumes it
While the game is paused, pacman and every ghost stay on their tiles
While the game is paused, nothing is eaten and no life is lost, even with a ghost on pacman's tile, and the frightened timer does not count down
Once resumed, pacman and the ghosts move again on the next step
A game that has been won or lost cannot be paused
While the game is paused the status line reads Paused and the score, lives and canvas do not change, including when P is pressed before the first direction key
Direction keys pressed while the game is paused are ignored and do not steer pacman after it resumes
When the game is won, the canvas shows YOU WIN and the final score
When the game is lost, the canvas shows GAME OVER and the final score
On the score screen, pressing any key, P included, starts a fresh running game with the score, lives and dots back at their starting values
The key that restarts the game does not steer pacman
A held-down key repeating, or a key pressed with Ctrl, Meta or Alt, does not restart the game
While the game is being played, the score is visible on the page as Score followed by the current points, and reads Score: 0 before anything is eaten
The score is shown in the same row as the lives, next to them
Eating a dot raises the displayed score by the points scoring gives a dot
Eating a power pellet raises the displayed score by the points scoring gives a power pellet
Eating a frightened ghost raises the displayed score by the points scoring gives a caught ghost
The score on the win and game-over screens equals the score the display showed on the last step
The fruit appears once half of the dots have been eaten, and not before
The fruit disappears when its time runs out without being eaten
Pacman reaching the fruit while it is showing eats it and removes it from the maze
Eating the fruit raises the score by more than a power pellet is worth
The fruit appears at most once per game, whether it was eaten or expired
Ready message at the start of each life
When a game starts, the canvas shows READY! in the maze
After a life is lost while lives remain, the canvas shows READY! in the maze
When the last life is lost, no READY! is shown and the game is lost
While READY! is showing, pacman and every ghost stay on their tiles, even when a direction is requested
When READY! ends, the message disappears and pacman and the ghosts move on the next step
Eaten ghosts return to the ghost house
A frightened ghost touched by pacman is eaten for points and starts returning from where it was eaten
A returning ghost is harmless and uneatable: touching pacman costs no life and scores nothing
Each tick a returning ghost advances one walkable step along a shortest path to its home cell in the ghost house, ignoring pacman
A returning ghost enters the ghost house through its door and, on reaching its home cell, resumes chasing
A power pellet eaten while a ghost is returning does not frighten that ghost, and it keeps returning
When frightened mode ends while a ghost is still returning, that ghost keeps returning while the other ghosts resume chasing
Losing a life or starting a new game puts every ghost, including a returning one, on its home cell chasing
A returning ghost is drawn in a colour different from chasing and frightened ghosts
Speed boost after a power pellet
Eating a power pellet starts a speed boost that applies from the next tick; eating an ordinary dot does not
While the boost is active pacman moves the boost multiplier of cells per tick, stopping at a wall, while ghosts still move one cell per tick
The boost lasts exactly the boost duration in ticks, after which pacman moves one cell per tick again
A power pellet eaten during a boost restores the full boost duration and does not add to the remaining time or raise the speed

Every cell pacman crosses during a boosted tick is resolved in turn: dots and fruit are eaten, a ghost met is eaten or costs a life, and pacman moves no further once the game is won or the life is lost
The boost does not count down while the game is paused or the ready message is showing
Losing a life or starting a new game ends any boost
The best score is kept for the tab session: after a run ends and the page is reloaded in the same tab, the best score is shown again
When a run ends in a win or a loss with a score higher than the best, or with no best yet, that score becomes the best
A run that ends with a score lower than or equal to the best leaves the best unchanged, and the best does not change while a run is still in play
When session storage is unavailable or holds an invalid value, the game still runs and the best score is kept in memory for the life of the page
The best score is displayed as text, and shows that no best exists yet until a run has ended
Starting a new game resets the score but not the displayed best score
No data shape without a migration path once real records exist
Personal data never leaves its declared store
Every AWS resource is tagged from birth
